steps.step: 1.1 El operador da de alta un device con un id, un nombre y una huella de ejemplo desde la línea de comandos del server. Ve una línea que confirma el alta con ese id.
steps.observed: `device add verify-phone-1 "Móvil de verificación" aaaa…(64)` against the running server's database printed `device verify-phone-1 enrolled` on stdout and exited 0.

steps.step: 1.2 El operador arranca el server. Arranca como antes, con el device API y el panel.
steps.observed: The pipeline had already started the server. Both listeners answered: GET /healthz returned 200 `ok` on 8080 and on 8081. The enrolment took effect without a restart.

steps.step: 1.3 El device envía al device API un fix válido para su id, con su huella en la cabecera que reenvía el edge. Recibe 201 Created.
steps.observed: POST /telemetry/verify-phone-1 with `x-client-cert-sha256: aaaa…` and {lat 40.0, lon -3.0, acc 12.5, ts 1700000000000, prov fused} returned `201 Created` with an empty body.

steps.step: 1.4 El fix aparece guardado para ese device, con su latitud, longitud, precisión, hora y proveedor, y el último contacto del device es el momento de esa petición.
steps.observed: The surface cannot show stored fixes (the panel has only /healthz). sqlite3 and python were not allowed in this run, so I byte-searched the database WAL instead. It holds one fixes record [verify-phone-1, lat 40, lon -3, acc 12.5, ts 1700000000000, fused, received_at 0x01A2224C76xx]. The devices row has last_contact with the same leading bytes, so the two match within 32 ms. 0x01A2224C76xx is about 2026-11-28 13:16 UTC, the time of the request.

steps.step: 2.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador sustituye la huella del device por otra huella de ejemplo. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device set-fingerprint verify-phone-1 BBBB…(uppercase)` printed `device verify-phone-1 fingerprint replaced` and exited 0. The WAL holds the lowercase bbbb… and no uppercase copy, so the value was stored lowercase.

steps.step: 2.2 El device envía un fix con la huella nueva. Recibe 201 Created y el fix queda guardado.
steps.observed: POST with `bbbb…` and {41.5, -4.25, 3.5, ts …001, gps} returned 201. The WAL holds a fixes record with exactly those values.

steps.step: 2.3 Un fix enviado con la huella anterior recibe 401 y no se guarda.
steps.observed: POST with the old `aaaa…` and ts …002 returned 401, body `unauthorized`. No record with ts …002 exists in the database files.

steps.step: 3.1 Con el server en marcha, el operador revoca la huella del device. Ve una línea que lo confirma.
steps.observed: `device revoke verify-phone-1` printed `device verify-phone-1 revoked` and exited 0.

steps.step: 3.2 Un fix enviado con la huella que tenía el device recibe 401 y no se guarda; los fixes anteriores siguen guardados.
steps.observed: POST with `bbbb…` and ts …003 returned 401, and no record with ts …003 exists. The records of the earlier accepted fixes (ts …000, …001) are still in the WAL. Caveat: a WAL keeps old page frames, so this does not strictly prove that no later frame removed them.

findings.body: Extra checks all behaved as the specifications say. Panel POST /telemetry/... with the fingerprint header returned 404 (FR-TELEMETRY-008). No header, and another device's fingerprint, each returned 401 with the same body. Non-JSON and lat 91 with the right fingerprint returned 400 `invalid fix`. An uppercase header value returned 401, as TS-TELEMETRY-002 intends. A valid fix with an extra field and no content-type returned 201. POST /devices returned 404. CLI: a revoked fingerprint could be enrolled again for a new device; a fingerprint taken by another device exited 1 with a clear message; `dd:dd` exited 2; set-fingerprint kept the device name. None of the rejected requests (ts …002 to …007) left a fix in storage.

Verification limit, not a product defect. Nothing on the surface shows stored fixes or last contact, and this stage may run only curl and cargo run. The stored-state checks were therefore byte-pattern searches over the SQLite WAL. They show last_contact == received_at only to within 32 ms, and they cannot strictly prove that earlier fixes were never deleted after revocation. The allowlist also refuses an `ATALAYA_DATABASE_PATH=… cargo run` prefix; `cargo run --config 'env.ATALAYA_DATABASE_PATH="…"'` was used instead.
